input: Reach out to my university career center for advice

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what specific type of advice they need (resume review, job search, interview prep, career switching, networking, etc.) determines what to ask for and which service to request.
Whether the user is a current student, recent alumni, or graduate student affects their eligibility for services and which office or person to contact.
Understanding where they are in their career journey (graduating soon, exploring options, just started a job search) shapes the urgency and angle of the outreach.
Whether they want to email, call, use an online booking portal, or walk in determines the immediate next action to take.
A deadline (e.g., upcoming application due date, graduation timeline) affects how quickly they need a response and how to frame the request.
Whether they prefer a one-on-one appointment, a group workshop, or written resources (e.g., templates, guides) affects what to ask the career center for.
Knowing what outcome they want from this interaction (a reviewed resume, a clearer career direction, a job referral, etc.) defines what 'done well' looks like and helps prioritize the ask.

gold.taskTitle: Reach out to university career center for advice
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to contact their university's career center to get professional guidance, but the purpose, method, timing, and specifics of what help they need are all unclear.

questions.title: What specific topic do you need career advice on?
questions.description: Identify the exact area of guidance needed — e.g., resume review, interview prep, job search strategy, career change, internship search, or networking.

questions.title: Are you a current student or a recent graduate?
questions.description: Determine the user's academic status, as this affects eligibility for career center services and which contacts or programs apply to them.

questions.title: Where are you right now in your job or career search?
questions.description: Understand the user's current stage — just starting to explore, actively applying, post-offer negotiation, etc. — to frame the outreach appropriately.

questions.title: How do you prefer to contact the career center?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants to send an email, book an appointment online, call, or drop in, so the immediate next step can be made concrete.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline driving the urgency of this outreach?
questions.description: Find out if there is a time-sensitive trigger — such as an application deadline, an upcoming interview, or graduation — that affects how quickly they need a response.

questions.title: Would you prefer an appointment, a workshop, or written resources?
questions.description: Determine the format of support the user wants — a personal one-on-one session, a group event, or self-service materials — so the right service can be requested.

questions.title: What would a successful outcome of this interaction look like?
questions.description: Define what 'done well' means — a polished resume, a clearer career direction, a list of job leads, a mock interview — so the ask to the career center can be focused and purposeful.
